subject: McGlynn Middle School Enrollment Imbalance
overview: The committee reviewed the McGlynn Middle School Action Plan to address socioeconomic disparities and analyzed district capacity relative to new real estate development. Members also referred a residency enrollment dispute to a private meeting and finalized the fiscal year 2017 financial close-out.

items.title: Approval of Minutes
items.summary: Approved the minutes of the September 11, 2017 meeting.

items.title: School Enrollment Dispute
items.summary: Referred a residency and enrollment dispute regarding two children to a private meeting between the family, legal counsel, and administration. Discussion focused on conflicting probate court rulings and the children's current attendance in North Andover.

items.title: School Supply and Backpack Donations
items.summary: Accepted reports on the 10th anniversary Team Medford supply drive and a donation of 60 filled backpacks from Agero.

items.title: Wegmans and Stop-and-Shop Reports
items.summary: Placed the Wegmans informational meeting report on file and tabled the Stop-and-Shop donation report.

items.title: MCAS 2.0 and Accountability Update
items.summary: Received a schedule for the October release of MCAS 2.0 results and accountability ratings, noting that districts must achieve a 90% participation rate to maintain assistance levels.

items.title: Summer Programs Recap
items.summary: Reviewed reports on various summer programs, highlighting 140 average weekly attendees at the Summer Fun program and the implementation of online credit recovery via Plato.

items.title: McGlynn Middle School Action Plan
items.summary: Discussed strategies to address significant socioeconomic and enrollment imbalances between middle schools, including shared staff, new reading assessments, and potential changes to school selection protocols. Administrators reported a 24% gap in free and reduced lunch rates between the two middle schools.

items.title: Real Estate Development Enrollment Impact
items.summary: Analyzed data showing that residents of eight major apartment complexes account for 2.4% of district enrollment, suggesting significant existing capacity in elementary and middle schools.

items.title: FY17 Financial Close Out
items.summary: Presented the final fiscal year 2017 report, identifying a $1.4 million variance to be applied to the fiscal year 2018 budget to offset reduced state reimbursements.

items.title: Houston Relief Drive and Resolutions
items.summary: Viewed a video documentation of the community sporting goods drive for Hurricane Harvey victims and approved memorial resolutions for several former staff members and public officials.
